If that cleanup fails, the pending directory remains; the next attempt sees both canonical and pending copies and permanently rejects the operation instead of reconciling the pending directory.

When both canonical and pending recovery copies exist, failure to remove the pending copy is logged with `eprintln!` and converted to `Ok(None)`. SyncBase then proceeds and can report success while cleanup has failed and the duplicate remains indefinitely, violating the fail-closed/error-propagation requirement.

`remove_tree_bounded` validates its byte, entry, and depth budgets while deletion is already in progress. If a late entry exceeds a limit, earlier siblings have already been removed, so a resource-limit error can partially destroy the canonical recovery slot. Complete a non-destructive bounded traversal before removing anything.

After atomically exchanging the active baseline, a failure or crash before promoting `replacement` leaves the prior baseline at this deterministic staging path. The next invocation unconditionally rejects the occupied path, permanently blocking cleanup without manual intervention. Reconcile or adopt interrupted published transactions safely on restart.

When both pending and canonical recovery directories exist, failure to remove the pending directory returns it as the sole staged copy even though the canonical slot was never staged. The caller can commit the new sync stamp and then clean only the pending directory, returning success while canonical recovery remains. Propagate reconciliation failure or track and clean both copies before allowing success.

`metadata.json` cannot distinguish the two interrupted states: it is present both in a fully prepared candidate before the exchange and in the prior active tree left at `replacement` after the exchange. A crash after `replace_tree` but before publication is therefore misclassified as a completed exchange, causing reconciliation to delete the canonical recovery slot and replace it with a candidate that was never active. Persist an explicit transaction phase and only promote the staging tree when the exchange is proven to have occurred.

The bounded preflight is followed by a separate destructive traversal that carries no depth or entry budget. If the workspace tree changes between or during the passes, newly inserted content is recursively traversed and deleted without the validated limits, potentially causing unbounded recursion or partial deletion before a later failure. Keep the budget enforced during the destructive traversal or remove a fixed, isolated snapshot.

The prepared-candidate phase marker is removed and that removal is synced before either parent directory containing the exchange is synced. A crash in this window can persist the marker deletion while losing the exchange, leaving the unpublished candidate at `replacement` without its marker. Startup then misclassifies it as the prior active tree and can delete the canonical recovery copy. Keep the marker until the exchange is durably committed, and preserve or recreate it whenever rollback leaves the candidate in staging.

Recovery renames `replacement` to the canonical slot and syncs it before the active phase marker is removed. A crash after reconciliation returns but before marker removal leaves no `replacement`; the next invocation therefore hits the `!had_replacement` branch and permanently rejects an otherwise valid recovered state. Make marker cleanup part of the same recoverable transaction or recognize the canonical recovered slot on restart.

The production portion of this module is 710 lines, exceeding the repository's hard maximum of 700; `bin/sotp verify module-size` fails on this file. Split the new recovery/publication helpers into the existing submodules so the architecture gate passes.

After the phase marker has been removed, failures syncing that removal call `restore_after_baseline_exchange`. If rollback succeeds but deleting the rolled-back candidate then fails, the candidate remains at `replacement` without its phase marker. The next invocation misclassifies it as the prior active tree and may replace the canonical recovery copy with an unpublished candidate. Recreate and persist the prepared marker after rollback, before attempting cleanup, so cleanup failure remains safely distinguishable.

The workspace denies `clippy::unwrap_used`, but this new test module uses `unwrap()` throughout without a local test-only allowance. Consequently an all-targets Clippy run will fail before these tests can pass; add the allowance used by `base_merge.rs::tests` or eliminate the unwraps.

`run_git(repo, args)?` and the following snapshot can fail after `git stash` has already mutated the worktree or `refs/stash`. A timeout/output-limit failure may therefore report `Unavailable` after a completed or partial push/pop, and a retry can operate on the wrong stash entry. Re-adjudicate stash and worktree state after runner or post-operation inspection failures, as the guarded merge path does.

The branch-ref snapshot is not lossless: `%(refname)=%(objectname)` omits symbolic-ref targets, while line 95 also converts raw ref bytes with `from_utf8_lossy`. Retargeting a symbolic branch between branches at the same commit can leave every snapshot field unchanged, so forbidden branch-ref drift is accepted. Include symbolic targets and compare lossless records/raw bytes; the added test only verifies ordinary stash behavior using the same incomplete representation.

The public zero-argument `new()` lacks a `Default` implementation. `clippy::new_without_default` is warn-by-default and workspace warnings are denied, so the all-targets Clippy gate fails. Implement `Default`, matching `FsGitWorkflowAdapter`, or remove the redundant constructor.

`type_signals_codec.rs` remains an unmerged Git path (stage 1/2/3 entries exist), despite no conflict markers in the working-tree text. The branch cannot be considered a resolved, buildable final merge until this path is resolved and staged normally.

Add a regression test creating same-named `refs/tags/<base>` and `refs/heads/<base>` refs, then verify the merge resolves the branch commit. Existing tests only cover the unambiguous case and would not detect a future reintroduction of the tag-precedence bug.

The new baseline freshness check reads rustdoc baselines through `read_text`, whose capability-exec limit is only 4 MiB, while type-signal evaluation supports baselines up to 64 MiB. The active infrastructure baseline is 10,362,686 bytes, so this rejects a valid current cache with `SourceUnavailable(ImplCatalog)` and makes the report unusable for normal tracks. Hash the baseline with the baseline-specific bounded byte reader/limit and add a regression test above 4 MiB.

The pre-existing-state checks are not atomic with `run_guarded_merge`: another process can create an unrelated merge/unmerged index state after lines 125–129 but before line 133. If the merge then fails, `adjudicate_merge_after_runner_error` returns `Conflicted` solely from the post-failure unmerged paths check (line 587), authorizing recovery for state this invocation did not create. The guarded operation needs serialization or provenance-aware/atomic state handling across the check and merge.

The preflight checks and `run_guarded_merge` are not atomic. Another process can create an unrelated merge/unmerged index state after lines 125–129 but before line 133; after the merge fails, lines 146–148 or 595–598 accept any `MERGE_HEAD` equal to the requested base and return `Conflicted`, even though this invocation did not create it. Serialize the guarded operation or use provenance/state handling that covers the entire check-to-adjudication window.

findings.category: symlink not rejected at boundary / lock bypass
findings.message: `acquire_base_merge_lock` performs `reject_symlinks_below(&lock_path, ...)` and then opens the path separately with `OpenOptions::open`. A concurrent replacement can swap `metadata.json.lock` to a symlink between these operations; `open` follows it, allowing the guarded-merge lock to target an attacker-selected file or bypass serialization. Open the lock with an atomic no-follow primitive (for example `O_NOFOLLOW`) and fail closed.

`--verify --quiet` exits 1 both when `MERGE_HEAD` is absent and when it exists but is malformed or cannot resolve to a commit. Treating every exit 1 as `None` lets the adapter start over pre-existing merge state instead of failing closed; the runner-error path can even adjudicate `Clean` when the base is already an ancestor. Detect raw `MERGE_HEAD` presence separately and reject invalid contents.

The post-lock branch read shadows the branch used to select the lock without comparing them. If HEAD changes from track A to track B in this window, validation can proceed against B while holding A's `metadata.json.lock`, so B's merge/metadata operations are not serialized. Reject any change from the locked branch or acquire the lock corresponding to the re-read branch.

The added production helpers increase this module to 726 non-test lines, exceeding the configured 700-line hard limit. `bin/sotp verify module-size` now fails for this file, so the new merge-state/locking implementation must be extracted into a sibling module.

This patch grows the production portion of the module to 764 lines, exceeding the configured 700-line hard limit. `bin/sotp verify module-size` fails on this file, so the new merge locking/state helpers must be extracted into a sibling module before the required gate can pass.

`read_snapshot_file` uses path-based `fs::File::open` without a no-follow/symlink recheck. After the earlier `symlink_metadata` validation, a concurrent replacement can turn the entry into a symlink and make this adapter follow it outside the trusted track tree during publication verification. Open the validated file descriptor with `O_NOFOLLOW` (or revalidate atomically) and read from that descriptor.

`open_snapshot_file_nofollow` protects only the final path component. `read_snapshot_file` still opens a path whose intermediate directories can be replaced concurrently with symlinks after `reject_symlinks_below` runs, causing traversal outside the trusted track tree. Use directory descriptors/openat-style traversal (or equivalent component-wise no-follow opens) for the full path.

The new descriptor-based leaf reads do not cover directory enumeration: `fs::read_dir(path)` is still performed after a path-based symlink check. If an intermediate directory is replaced concurrently, `read_dir` can follow that symlink and enumerate outside the trusted track tree. Traverse directories using already-open directory descriptors with `openat(..., NOFOLLOW)` as well, or fail closed on the replacement.

The handle-relative traversal begins with `open_snapshot_directory_nofollow(root)`, which opens the root by pathname. `O_NOFOLLOW` protects only the final `root` component; a concurrent replacement of an ancestor such as `track/items` or the recovery parent with a symlink can redirect this open outside the trusted tree before descriptor traversal begins. Open each snapshot root relative to an already validated parent directory descriptor (or otherwise verify the complete component chain atomically).

A matching MERGE_HEAD does not prove Git reported a conflict. The runner can fail after a clean merge has written MERGE_HEAD and produced a fully merged index but before committing; the new test itself constructs this no-unmerged-path state. Returning Conflicted skips required clean-merge cleanup and incorrectly authorizes /track:recover. Require both a matching MERGE_HEAD and unmerged paths; otherwise fail closed.

The drift check and RENAME_EXCHANGE are separate operations without a lock. A writer can update a non-baseline file after verification returns but before the exchange; that edit moves into the recovery tree and is later deleted after SyncBase succeeds. The same gap permits the prepared tree to be replaced after its no-follow scan. Hold the applicable writer lock across verification and exchange, or provide equivalent atomic revalidation/rollback.

The advisory metadata.json.lock does not close the verification/exchange race for the non-baseline writers this check is meant to protect. Track artifact writers use other locks or none; the added ConcurrentWriteBaselineCapture itself successfully writes after this lock has been acquired. If such a write occurs after verification returns and before RENAME_EXCHANGE, it is moved to recovery and eventually deleted. The exchange needs atomic revalidation/rollback or a lock actually shared by every relevant writer.

TRACK_WRITER_LOCK_FILE is skipped by basename at every recursion depth, although only the track-root metadata.json.lock is the reserved writer lock. A legitimate nested file such as artifacts/metadata.json.lock is omitted from the replacement and also ignored by drift verification, so publication succeeds and permanently deletes it. Restrict the exception to the root-relative lock path.

Post-exchange verification can itself discard concurrent writes. A writer updating the new active tree after `EXCHANGE` causes a mismatch; rollback then moves that updated tree to `replacement` and deletes it. A writer holding an old-tree descriptor can likewise write after verification and lose the update when recovery is pruned. The advisory metadata lock does not exclude non-metadata writers. Publication needs synchronization shared by all artifact writers or reconciliation that preserves both trees.

The verification ignores more files than publication intentionally replaces: every `*-baseline.json` and every nested phase-marker name. Only generated root `*-types-baseline.json` files and the root transaction marker are intentional outputs. Consequently, a concurrent update to an ordinary file such as `custom-baseline.json` or a nested marker is invisible to both checks and can be overwritten by the stale snapshot. Restrict exemptions to the exact generated root paths.

The generated-baseline classifier does not match the binding contract. A valid `catalogue_file: "shared.json"` produces `shared-baseline.json`, but this predicate only recognizes `*-types-baseline.json`. The stale file therefore remains in the detached track, baseline capture sees an existing valid file and skips recapture, and cleanup republishes a baseline from the old state instead of the requested base commit. Conversely, any unconfigured root `*-types-baseline.json` is silently deleted. Derive the exact generated filenames from the resolved bindings, plus the feature baseline, instead of using a suffix heuristic.

Retaining both trees after post-exchange drift only postpones loss of writes made through an old-tree descriptor. On the next run, `reconcile_interrupted_replacement` promotes that divergent tree to the recovery slot, but a successful retry subsequently removes the slot before promoting its new recovery tree. The old-tree-only update is never merged into the active snapshot and is ultimately deleted. Recovery must reconcile or explicitly preserve divergent content until incorporated, or publication must use a lock shared by every artifact writer.

`expected` と `candidate` は `recovery_root` の直接の子として検証されていますが、比較用ディレクトリハンドルは `recovery_root.parent()` に対して開かれています。スナップショット処理はこのハンドルから各パスの basename を `openat` するため、実在する `recovery_root/.replacement` ではなくその親直下の `.replacement` を探して常に失敗します。その結果、既存 recovery slot がある再試行・promotion は内容が一致していても復旧不能になります。ここでは `recovery_root` 自体を開き、一致する二つのコピーを正常に昇格できるテストを追加してください。

`_writer_lock` は baseline replacement 関数内だけで保持され、return 時に解放された後、別の `write_sync_base_record` 呼び出しが recovery slot を移動・削除します。この隙間で別の base-merge が同じロックを取得して新しい baseline/recovery を publish すると、先行処理が古い base commit の SyncBase record を書き、新しい処理の recovery copy を削除できます。active baseline・authoritative stamp・recovery が異なる transaction に由来するデータ破損状態になるため、baseline publication から SyncBase commit/recovery cleanup まで同じロックで直列化するか、再取得後に recovery と request の世代を検証してください。

The unconditional staging/removal of every retained recovery slot can delete the only copy of a concurrent write. If the post-exchange drift check previously detected a write to the old active tree, publication deliberately retained that divergent `replacement`; on retry, `reconcile_interrupted_replacement` moves it to `recovery_slot`, but this path then stages and ultimately deletes it after installing a snapshot that lacks the write. Only bypass equivalence checks for slots proven to originate from a completed baseline publication followed by a later cleanup-stage failure; otherwise preserve the divergent slot.

Marker absence does not prove that a retained `replacement` is safe to supersede. Publication can remove the active marker successfully and then fail while syncing the track or parent directory; `retain_after_baseline_exchange` preserves both trees because a writer holding a pre-exchange descriptor may have changed the old tree during that window. On retry, passing `false` here lets reconciliation move that unique tree into the canonical slot, after which promotion deletes it without an equivalence check. Preserve or compare retained post-exchange trees using stronger provenance, including marker-cleared failure/crash states.

This unconditional error also classifies an ordinary crash immediately after the atomic exchange as unrecoverable: that valid state has an unmarked old tree in `replacement` and the phase marker in the new active tree. Every retry observes the same two paths and returns the same error, contradicting the transaction's documented restart reconciliation. Compare the two trees and reconcile equal content while preserving only divergent content instead of treating marker presence alone as a permanent stop condition.

The added recovery verification leaves this module at 731 production lines before `#[cfg(test)]`, exceeding the repository's hard 700-line limit; `bin/sotp verify module-size` now fails on this file. Extract the reconciliation/verification logic into a sibling module so the structural gate passes.

A markerless replacement proves only that the atomic exchange completed; it does not prove the retained trees are equivalent. If the post-exchange comparison detects a write through a pre-exchange descriptor into `replacement`, `retain_after_baseline_exchange` deliberately preserves both trees. On retry, this unconditional promotion skips that comparison, rebuilds from `active_track`, and eventually deletes the recovery slot after SyncBase, silently losing the retained write. Reconcile only expected telemetry differences and continue failing closed on other active/replacement divergence.

`atomic_write_file` replaces the retained telemetry file after both logs were snapshotted. `retain_after_baseline_exchange` explicitly allows a writer with a pre-exchange descriptor to keep appending to this retained tree, but such writers do not share the metadata lock. An append after the read at line 504—or through the old descriptor after this rename—is written to an inode that this replacement unlinks; the subsequent comparison can then pass while the appended event is silently lost. Synchronize with telemetry writers or reconcile without replacing the live append-only file.

The retained descriptor remains live after reconciliation, but the same retry later stages and deletes its recovery slot. An append through that descriptor after `reconcile_interrupted_replacement` returns exists only in `recovery_slot`; the new replacement is built from `active_track` without it, and this cleanup removes the sole copy (with later descriptor writes going to an unlinked inode). Reconcile or freeze the slot immediately before superseding it, or use synchronization shared by telemetry writers.

Renaming the hard link over `target` unlinks the target inode without synchronizing telemetry writers. A writer that opened the post-exchange active telemetry file before reconciliation can append after the snapshots or rename through that old descriptor; the append then exists only on the unlinked inode while subsequent checks read the source-linked path and pass. Establish the shared telemetry inode before the directory exchange or synchronize reconciliation with telemetry writers.

On Unix, if `source` and `target` already reference the same inode, renaming the newly created hard link over `target` succeeds as a no-op and leaves `.sotp-telemetry-link` behind. The new promotion flow reaches this state when active telemetry is already linked to retained recovery; the staging file is then copied into a later replacement, whose next reconciliation fails permanently at the existing-path check. Detect identical inodes and remove/skip the staging link, and reconcile orphaned staging entries on retries.

Non-telemetry equality is checked before the retained tree is promoted, but a writer holding a pre-exchange descriptor can modify that tree after the check. The next replacement is built from `active_track`, and this cleanup deletes the recovery slot containing the only copy of that late write. Synchronize all track writers or preserve the recovery slot until old-tree descriptors cannot introduce unmerged content.

The source and target paths are checked for symlinks only before the mutation, then `hard_link` and `rename` resolve them again by pathname. A concurrent replacement of either `logs` directory with a symlink can therefore create a hard link or overwrite `telemetry.jsonl` outside the trusted root. Perform these operations relative to no-follow directory descriptors (`linkat`/`renameat`) instead of re-resolving validated paths.

`append_file_in_place` validates the parent and file by pathname, but subsequently opens the path after another process can replace an intermediate directory with a symlink. `O_NOFOLLOW` protects only the final component, so the append can corrupt a file outside `trusted_root`. Open each component relative to a trusted no-follow directory descriptor and append through that descriptor.

When `had_recovery` is true, non-telemetry verification compares only `active_track` with the current `replacement`; it never compares `recovery_slot`. A write through a descriptor to the earlier retained tree after `reconcile_interrupted_replacement`'s comparison follows that tree into `recovery_slot`, and this staging/cleanup path then deletes its only copy. Verify the recovery slot's non-baseline content before staging it or synchronize every writer that can retain an old-tree descriptor.

Telemetry reconciliation runs after `verify_non_baseline_content_matches`, even though that comparison includes `logs/telemetry.jsonl`. An ordinary append made after the replacement snapshot was copied therefore aborts publication before the code can establish the shared inode; because telemetry writers do not share this lock, recurring telemetry can continually block cleanup. Reconcile telemetry before the comparison, then fail closed on remaining non-telemetry drift.

The retry path unconditionally deletes the retained recovery tree's `.sync-base.json` before comparing it with the new replacement. If a previous valid stamp exists in both trees and a later SyncBase-stage operation fails, the next retry removes only the recovery copy, so the comparison at line 558 necessarily fails and the retry cannot converge. This also mutates the recovery tree before subsequent validation can fail.

Production code treats the test-only root file `failure-telemetry.json` as append-only telemetry, although the actual telemetry contract uses `logs/telemetry.jsonl`. Any legitimate non-baseline artifact with this name is rewritten and hard-linked before drift verification, allowing prefix-related changes to bypass the fail-closed comparison. Remove this special case and make the regression test use the real telemetry path.

Replacing the secondary telemetry entry with a hard link unlinks its previous inode. A `TelemetryWriter` already holding that secondary file open continues appending to the now-unlinked inode, so records written after reconciliation disappear when the descriptor closes. This occurs during retained-recovery promotion when the active track is reconciled as the secondary; reconciliation must coordinate writers or avoid replacing a potentially live inode.

`telemetry_path_is_open` only scans `/proc/self/fd`, although the telemetry writer explicitly supports multi-process appends, and the scan is also racy with the later target rename. An external writer—or a writer that appends/closes between the snapshot and scan—can therefore be missed; replacing the secondary path then leaves subsequent writes on an unlinked inode and loses telemetry. Reconciliation must coordinate with all writers or avoid replacing a potentially writable target inode.

Adding `.sync-base.json` to the ignored-file set does not handle the supported failure case where that path is a directory: snapshot comparison applies ignored names only after the directory branch has already recursed. After a SyncBase failure preserves such a directory in recovery and the operator removes the active obstruction, every retry compares the retained directory against a replacement without it and fails permanently. The retry comparison must ignore or reconcile the top-level path regardless of node type.

Interrupted reconciliation still calls `reconcile_telemetry_inode` with `preserve_secondary = false`. If telemetry did not exist before the directory exchange but a long-lived `TelemetryWriter` creates the active file before a post-exchange failure, retry sees `(primary=None, secondary=Some)`, copies its bytes, and replaces the active entry with the primary inode. The writer retains the unlinked old inode, so subsequent events disappear. Preserve the active secondary inode or synchronize with telemetry writers.

The retained `.sync-base.json` is copied directly into the markerless `replacement` before recovery staging and promotion. If the process crashes or a later staging/rename operation fails, that modified replacement remains; on restart, `reconcile_interrupted_replacement` compares it against an active tree without the marker and fails before this normalization is reached again. This leaves the retry permanently blocked. Normalize through recoverable staging or record a phase that restart can reconcile.

The new recovery comparison remains a point-in-time check. A writer holding a descriptor to any non-telemetry file in the pre-exchange tree can append after verification; the following staging and cleanup delete that tree's sole link while active and replacement contain only the earlier snapshot. The append and all later descriptor writes are silently lost. Synchronize these writers or retain/merge the old recovery tree instead of deleting it after an unlocked comparison.

`link_telemetry_inode` unconditionally unlinks the fixed name `logs/.sotp-telemetry-link`. During interrupted reconciliation the target parent is the live active track, so a pre-existing non-baseline artifact with that name is deleted before drift verification; a later error does not restore it. Use collision-safe staging or remove an existing entry only after verifying it is an orphan created by this operation.

The previous recovery tree is deliberately retained at promotion so open descriptors remain reachable, but the immediately following SyncBase call invokes this helper again with both the pending tree and canonical slot present. This branch unconditionally deletes the pending tree, so descriptor-backed writes after promotion are unlinked and lost; the new regression test stops before SyncBase and misses this path. Reconcile or preserve the retained tree through SyncBase instead of deleting it.

`link_telemetry_inode` relies on `renameat` to consume its staging hard link, but interrupted-publication retries normally have source and target telemetry already pointing to the same inode. POSIX rename then succeeds as a no-op, leaving `.sotp-telemetry-link-0` in the active tree; the subsequent non-baseline comparison sees the extra file and permanently blocks recovery. Detect identical inodes or explicitly remove the owned staging name after the rename.

When a markerless replacement is reconciled while a canonical recovery slot exists and the base staging directory is absent, the old slot is staged with `preserve == false` and deleted here immediately after installing the replacement. A process holding a descriptor to that prior recovery tree is then left writing to an unlinked inode, silently losing later writes—the same descriptor case `promote_baseline_recovery_slot` now explicitly preserves. Reconciliation must retain or safely merge that staged tree too.

After one failed SyncBase leaves the base pending directory, every later successful SyncBase selects a fresh `.sotp-baseline-recovery-current-<id>-N` path with `preserve == true`, and this early return prevents any generation from being removed. Each subsequent base merge therefore retains another complete recovery tree until disk exhaustion or the 10,000-name limit permanently blocks SyncBase. Add bounded reclamation/reconciliation that still protects live descriptors.

The post-rename unlink handles the successful same-inode case, but a crash or error after `linkat` and before that unlink leaves `.sotp-telemetry-link-N` behind. During interrupted-publication reconciliation this staging file is created inside the active track; the next retry skips it, creates another candidate, and then fails the non-baseline comparison on the original extra file indefinitely. Existing owned staging links must be recognized and reconciled on restart.

A single failed SyncBase leaves the base retained directory; the next two baseline publications permanently retain `current-0` and `current-1`, and no path ever reclaims them. Every later publication with a canonical recovery slot therefore hits this limit and fails before SyncBase—even when the stamp value is an idempotent no-op—and retries cannot self-heal without manual deletion. The bounded policy needs a safe reconciliation/reclamation path rather than a permanent two-generation dead end.

`retain_open_file_inodes` always allocates a new `inode-N` hardlink for every regular file in every reclaimed generation, even when that inode is already retained, and nothing removes these links. Successful cleanup therefore consumes the fixed 10,000-name namespace cumulatively (later merges can retain two whole track trees); once it fills, all subsequent base-merge cleanups fail permanently with `retained descriptor link limit reached`. Deduplicate retained device/inode pairs or provide a bounded lifecycle that cannot exhaust across normal retries.

The new device/inode check only deduplicates retries of the same staged inode. Each successful baseline generation normally creates fresh file inodes, and this function still adds permanent hardlinks for all of them while nothing removes `.sotp-retained-recovery-descriptors-*`. Once the cumulative 10,000-link namespace fills, cleanup returns `retained descriptor link limit reached`; the staged tree remains, so every later merge retries the same failing reclamation and cannot complete. Provide a bounded lifecycle for obsolete generations instead of retaining every distinct inode forever.

When a descriptor-retention directory already exists, this function deletes it before linking the current generation. A writer can keep an older staged file descriptor open across another cleanup; deleting its last hardlink makes subsequent writes unreachable and permanently lost when that descriptor closes. The current test drops the writer before the next generation, so it misses this case. Preserve prior retained inodes while adding the new generation, or use a lifecycle that proves no older descriptors remain before unlinking them.

The stable per-relative-path link retains only the first inode. If a later recovery generation has the same path and an open writer, the existing target makes this function skip linking the newer inode; cleanup then removes its staging tree, so subsequent writes through that descriptor become unreachable and are lost. Each current/live inode must remain recoverable, not only the oldest inode at that path.

The per-call entry and byte limits do not bound the persistent retained-descriptor tree: every newly encountered relative path adds a permanent hardlink, and existing retained content is never counted or reclaimed. Repeated merges with path churn can therefore grow disk and inode usage without bound.

Keeping a permanent target entry for each relative path makes ordinary file-to-directory or directory-to-file changes fail cleanup. A later generation encounters the previous entry type, returns an error, and subsequent cleanup retries hit the same persistent conflict, preventing base-merge recovery from progressing.

`reclaim_current_staging_paths` unconditionally deletes every retained `current-*` generation before allocating the next one. A failed SyncBase can deliberately leave one of these paths as the only link to that generation; if an open descriptor remains after the corresponding active file was replaced or removed, the next retry unlinks its inode and subsequent writes become irretrievable. A fixed generation count cannot safely bound descriptor lifetime this way.

The hard-link replacement protocol is not crash-idempotent. When source and target already reference the same inode, POSIX rename is a no-op, leaving `.sotp-telemetry-link-*` present until the following unlink. A crash in that window can leave the extra entry inside a markerless replacement; restart verifies tree equality before re-entering this helper, so the unexpected entry makes every reconciliation retry fail.

The new baseline validation uses unbounded `std::fs::read`, allowing an oversized baseline file to exhaust verifier memory and bypassing the repository's bounded-I/O policy. Read the baseline through the existing limited reader with the established rustdoc-baseline size cap.

The new branch implementation-input hashing performs unbounded subprocess collection: `git_ls_tree_recursive_regular_files` calls `Command::output()` for the entire recursive `git ls-tree` result before enforcing `MAX_SOURCE_FILES`, and each listed blob is likewise fully buffered by `git_show_blob` before `required_blob_limited` applies its size/budget checks. A branch containing many source paths or an oversized blob can therefore exhaust memory or block the merge gate before the intended limits take effect. Stream the git output or enforce bounded subprocess output before collecting it.

The explicit `signal check-impl-catalog` path now requires local layer baselines, and `current_implementation_input_hash` additionally requires `tddd-features-baseline.json`. All `track/items/**/*-baseline.json` files are intentionally gitignored, and this active track has none tracked. A fresh PR checkout therefore fails the track-aware CI gate before any hash comparison. The workflow must provision the authoritative baselines before this gate or use an authority available in fresh CI without trusting the cache itself.

`read_type_baseline_hash` fetches `<layer>-types-baseline.json` from `origin/<branch>`, but these snapshots are explicitly not version-controlled. New tracks therefore return `NotFound` and are always blocked by the merge gate. Force-tracking is not sufficient: Git output is capped at 16 MiB while the current usecase baseline is 18,065,236 bytes and local baseline readers permit 64 MiB. Read the authoritative local baseline with trusted-root, symlink, and compatible size guards, or coherently change the artifact lifecycle.

`branch_features` requires `tddd-features-baseline.json` from the remote branch, although the repository's baseline ignore rule prevents that file from being pushed. Consequently `read_type_implementation_input_hash` always returns `FetchError` for normal new tracks even if the type-baseline reader is fixed. Obtain the feature baseline from its actual authoritative location or introduce a committed attestation while preserving the declaration/baseline equality check.

`evaluate_layer_catalogue` accepts the cached document after checking only declaration and baseline hashes. A source, manifest, lockfile, toolchain, or feature-selection change can therefore leave this public Stage-2 verifier green on stale Blue signals, violating the three-hash freshness contract. Compute and compare the current implementation-input hash here before returning the document, failing closed on acquisition errors.

A malformed present feature-authority path is treated as structural absence: `is_file()` returns false for a directory or broken symlink, so the implementation-input freshness check is skipped and a stale cached signal document can pass. Probe the path with the symlink/regular-file boundary and fail closed for any present-but-invalid authority.

Any failure from `nightly_toolchain_identifier` is treated as authority absence and silently skips implementation-input freshness validation. This includes unreadable/failed toolchain acquisition in a local workspace, allowing stale cached signals to pass; only genuine structural absence should downgrade the check, while acquisition failures must fail closed.

`check_impl_catalog_from_signals_file` accepts `baseline_path` but only rejects symlinks; it does not verify the path is contained within `workspace_root`, allowing an outside regular file to influence freshness checks. Normalize and enforce trusted-root containment before reading it.

When `tddd-features-baseline.json` is absent, this early return skips `implementation_input_hash` verification entirely. Fresh CI checkouts intentionally lack baseline files, but AC-07/AC-09 require such contexts to verify both committed authorities; the committed feature declaration still permits recomputing the implementation hash, as the branch-side helper already does. Consequently, source, Cargo, lockfile, toolchain, or committed feature changes can leave stale type signals while this validation gate passes. Recompute from the committed feature declaration when the local feature baseline is structurally absent, and fail closed if another required input cannot be read.

The fresh-checkout fallback still unconditionally calls `hash_workspace_inputs`, which requires `rustup run nightly rustc -Vv`. Track CI runs `signal check-impl-catalog` inside the stable-only container that explicitly lacks the nightly toolchain, so production CI will fail with an indeterminate implementation-input hash even when all committed authorities match; the unit tests mask this via the `#[cfg(test)]` toolchain-identity fixture. Provision and pin the matching nightly toolchain for this gate, or provide a committed-authority hashing path that does not depend on unavailable local toolchain state.

The default `track/items` case is eventually anchored to the repository root, but this earlier check inspects `<cwd>/track/items`. When invoked from a repository subdirectory, an unrelated symlink or non-directory `track` entry there makes `emit_active` fail and silently drops the required completion event even though `<repo>/track/items` is valid. Validate only the repository-root-anchored path for the default case.

This test depends on the ambient repository and branch, silently skips on non-track branches, and overwrites the real active track's `telemetry.jsonl`. Restoring the saved bytes can discard telemetry appended concurrently. Use a temporary Git repository and track branch so the test is independent and cannot corrupt workspace diagnostics.

`bounded_read_utf8_file` applies the capability-definition limit of 4 MiB, but valid rustdoc baselines are accepted up to 64 MiB. The current track already contains matching baselines between 5.9 MiB and 18.4 MiB, so this branch marks them unavailable and permanently renders `—` despite fresh cache hashes. Use a symlink-safe reader or streaming hash with the baseline limit, and cover a matching baseline larger than 4 MiB.

`read_catalogue_bytes` checks the file size with metadata, then calls `std::fs::read`, which reads to EOF without a bound. If the catalogue grows after the metadata check, it can bypass the 16 MiB limit and cause unbounded allocation in the pre-review gate. Open the file once and read through `take(MAX_TYPE_CATALOGUE_BYTES + 1)`, rejecting the extra byte, as `type_signals_evaluator::inputs::read_bytes_file_limited` does.

`read_signals` checks only a metadata snapshot and then uses `std::fs::read`, so a regular file that grows after the check can bypass `MAX_TYPE_SIGNALS_BYTES`. It also never requires a regular file, allowing a FIFO or device to block or stream without the intended bound. Open the file once, validate its opened metadata, read through `take(MAX_TYPE_SIGNALS_BYTES + 1)`, and reject the extra byte, as the corrected catalogue reader does.

Path dependencies that resolve outside the workspace (absolute paths or `..` traversal beyond the workspace root) are silently omitted from the implementation-input closure. A target can therefore depend on external source whose changes alter rustdoc semantics without changing the cached implementation hash, allowing stale signals to be reused. Reject such dependencies fail-closed instead of treating them as absent.

Dependency manifests are read before their parent path is symlink-checked. `read_regular_source_file` rejects only a symlink at the final `Cargo.toml`; a symlinked crate directory can therefore make this loader read and parse a file outside the trusted workspace before `workspace_source_root` later rejects it. Run `reject_symlinks_up_to_root` before the first manifest read.

The closure ignores root `[patch.*]` and `[replace]` path overrides. This repository already resolves infrastructure's registry dependency on `conch-parser` through `vendor/conch-parser`; changing that vendor source leaves the current hash unchanged even though Cargo's compilation input changed. Include effective local overrides and their transitive sources/manifests. See the [Cargo override semantics](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/overriding-dependencies.html).

A path inherited with `workspace = true` is returned without retaining that it came from the root manifest, then always resolved relative to the consuming crate. For example, workspace `domain = { path = "libs/domain" }` inherited by usecase is incorrectly resolved as `libs/usecase/libs/domain`, blocking valid Cargo workspaces. Resolve inherited paths relative to the workspace root. See [Cargo path and workspace dependency semantics](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/specifying-dependencies.html).

The added closure implementation raises the production portion of this module to 797 lines. `bin/sotp verify module-size` now fails because the repository maximum is 700 production lines. Extract the manifest/dependency-closure logic into a sibling module.

`queue_local_override_roots` only hashes overrides whose package is declared directly by the target or an already-loaded local manifest. Cargo patches/replacements can affect transitive registry dependencies, so a local `[patch.crates-io] bar = { path = "vendor/bar" }` used through registry dependency `foo` is never queued; edits under `vendor/bar` then leave the implementation hash unchanged. Aliased patch entries using `package = "bar"` are similarly indexed under the alias rather than the actual package. Conservatively queue every workspace-local override root or derive usage from Cargo's resolved graph.

The dependency manifests are parsed, but their declared source/build paths are ignored: every dependency is hashed only under `<root>/src` and at `<root>/build.rs`. Cargo permits inputs such as `[lib] path = "api.rs"` and `[package] build = "tools/build.rs"`; changing those compiled files after the manifest is stable can therefore leave both local and branch implementation hashes unchanged, allowing stale rustdoc signals to be reused. Derive these paths from each dependency manifest or hash a bounded, symlink-safe crate tree consistently on both paths.

`collect_declared_source_file` hashes only the manifest-declared crate-root file. A custom target such as `[lib] path = "api.rs"` can load sibling modules (`mod child;` → `child.rs`) outside `src/`; changing those modules leaves both local and branch implementation hashes unchanged, allowing stale rustdoc signals. Hash a bounded, symlink-safe source tree for custom targets rather than only the entry file.

The `allow_missing_source_tree` argument is inverted relative to the local implementation. Passing `source_paths.is_empty()` means the branch reader silently accepts a missing `src/` when no alternate source is declared, but rejects a valid custom-path crate with no `src/`. This breaks fail-closed acquisition and local/branch compatibility; pass `!source_paths.is_empty()` for both target and dependency calls.

Only the build-script entry file is hashed. Cargo compiles build scripts as Rust targets, so a normal `build.rs` may contain `mod helper;` with `helper.rs` beside it. Changing that helper can alter generated code or `rustc-cfg` output—and therefore rustdoc—without changing any currently hashed component. Collect each target and dependency build script's bounded, symlink-safe source tree in both local and branch paths.

`manifest_input_paths` represents both Cargo's optional auto-detected `build.rs` and an explicitly declared `package.build = "tools/build.rs"` identically, after which both readers treat NotFound as an optional absence. A missing explicitly declared build script is an unavailable authoritative input and must fail closed; preserve whether the path was explicit and use required-file acquisition for that case in both local and branch hashing.

Custom build scripts only add their containing directory to the implementation-input hash. A valid `build = "tools/build.rs"` can compile `#[path = "../build_support.rs"] mod build_support;`; changing that helper can alter rustdoc output without changing either hash. Hash the crate-bounded build-script source closure, or conservatively the crate tree.

A workspace-root path dependency normalizes to an empty crate root, making its default build-script path `build.rs` and `source_dir` empty here. The git helper converts that to the invalid pathspec `/`, so even an absent optional build script makes branch hashing fail while local hashing succeeds. Handle root-directory traversal explicitly.

The production portion of this module is now 711 lines. Consequently, `bin/sotp verify module-size` fails against the repository's 700-line maximum. Split the new input-discovery or acquisition logic into a submodule.

For a normal crate without an explicit target path or build script, only `<crate>/src` is collected. Valid Rust source can reference a crate-root module such as `#[path = "../public.rs"] mod public;`; changing `public.rs` can change the dependency's rustdoc API while leaving both implementation hashes unchanged. Collect the crate-bounded source closure for ordinary targets as well.

When a workspace-root package has a build script, `crate_directory` is the workspace root and this recursively hashes the raw filesystem, including `.git`, `target`, and ignored/untracked files. Branch hashing enumerates only committed Git entries, so a valid root path dependency with `build.rs` cannot produce byte-compatible local and branch hashes and may exceed traversal limits locally. Exclude repository metadata/build outputs or use an equivalent bounded input authority on both sides.

The local collector recursively hashes every regular file under each crate directory, whereas the branch collector sees only committed Git blobs. Git-ignored or unrelated untracked files therefore affect only the local hash; the current workspace already contains `libs/infrastructure/tmp/reviewer-runtime/*`, whose changing logs can both invalidate an evaluation mid-run and guarantee a merge-gate mismatch. Use the same authoritative source-file selection for local and branch hashing.

The compiled-source closure is bounded to the package directory without detecting sources loaded from outside it. Valid Rust such as `#[path = "../../shared_api.rs"] mod shared_api;` or an equivalent build-script module/include can affect rustdoc while residing elsewhere in the workspace; changing that file leaves this implementation hash unchanged and permits stale signals to be reused. Such referenced sources must be hashed or rejected fail-closed.

The reference scanner searches raw source text, so markers inside comments and string literals are treated as Rust syntax. For example, the current `build_inputs.rs` contains escaped `#[path = \"...\"]` fixture text; hashing the real infrastructure crate reaches that text and returns `source reference ... is not resolvable`, preventing both local and branch hashes from being produced. Parse Rust tokens and ignore non-code occurrences.

`rsplit_once(')')` selects the final closing parenthesis in the entire remaining source, not the matching end of `concat!`. A valid reference followed by code such as `println!("x")` therefore appends later string literals to the path and loads a nonexistent/wrong input. The parser needs balanced token-tree parsing.

Reference traversal stops for every file whose name does not end in `.rs`. Rust permits `include!("generated.inc")`; if that file contains another `include!`, the nested source is compiled but never added to the hash, allowing its changes to reuse stale signals.

A missing `src/` is nominally accepted when Cargo declares an explicit target path, but the code immediately calls `read_dir` on that missing directory anyway. The branch collector similarly hard-codes `allow_missing_source_tree = false` for the subsequent scan, so valid crates using `[lib] path = "api.rs"` without `src/` cannot produce either implementation hash.

`source_marker_positions` is not token-correct for valid Rust: it treats the `"` inside a character literal such as `const QUOTE: char = '"';` as the start of a string and reports an unterminated string, and it can match `include!` inside a longer macro name such as `myinclude!`. Either case can make implementation-input hashing unavailable for a compilable crate; use a Rust-aware lexer or handle character literals and token boundaries explicitly.

Literal references written with raw strings are rejected because the argument parser accepts only a leading ordinary double quote. Valid forms such as `include!(r#"generated.inc"#)` or `#[path = r"module.rs"]` therefore return `source reference ... is not resolvable` and block both local and branch hashing.

The `concat!` parser silently concatenates only double-quoted fragments and ignores other supported literal tokens. For example, Rust resolves `concat!("..", '/', "config.toml")` to `../config.toml`, while this code records `..config.toml`; if that wrong path exists, the actual external input can change without changing the implementation hash. Reject unsupported components or evaluate every supported literal exactly.

The crate-root scan still excludes every file without an `.rs` extension before validating manifest-declared target and build-script paths. Cargo target paths are filenames and may be extensionless, so valid declarations such as `[lib] path = "api"` or `build = "tools/build"` are reported as outside the bounded selection; the branch collector mirrors the same restriction.

`concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), ...)` is not resolved with Rust's byte-concatenation semantics. The parser discards the manifest-directory component and resolves all remaining literals beneath `crate_root`; for example, a suffix `"-data.bin"` actually names a sibling of the crate directory, while this code hashes a child inside it. If both paths exist, changes to the file compiled by Rust do not change the implementation-input hash.

Source-reference resolution unconditionally converts backslashes to `/`. On Unix a backslash is a valid filename character, so a raw reference such as `r"../../../shared\asset.bin"` can make rustc read `shared\asset.bin` while the evaluator hashes `shared/asset.bin`. With both files present, the cache and merge gate can accept stale signals.

The collector infers `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` from each referenced file's physical path. Included Rust is expanded in the including crate's compilation context, even when the included file lies outside that crate or under another workspace crate. Such a file can therefore reference the target crate's asset while this lookup hashes the workspace root's or another crate's asset instead.

Every UTF-8 component is recursively parsed as Rust source, although the component set includes arbitrary files under `src` and opaque `include_str!`/`include_bytes!` targets. Valid assets containing an unmatched quote/comment or text resembling `include!(...)` can consequently make implementation-input acquisition fail or load an unrelated path. The closure needs to retain whether a component is executable Rust source versus opaque data.

The branch traversal materializes the complete recursive `git ls-tree` result before applying any entry bound, and the caller only limits files that survive the Rust/source filters. A branch can contain arbitrarily many non-Rust entries beneath a crate, causing unbounded output allocation and work while also diverging from the local collector's `MAX_SOURCE_ENTRIES` fail-closed behavior.

The branch blob limits are enforced only after `required_blob`/`fetch_blob_safe` has buffered the complete `git show` output. Thus a blob far larger than `MAX_SOURCE_FILE_BYTES` or `MAX_DECLARATION_BYTES` can exhaust memory before the advertised cap is checked; the blob size must be bounded before or while reading.

Source-reference discovery only recognizes the exact textual forms `include!`, `include_str!`, `include_bytes!`, and `#[path`. Valid Rust forms such as `include ! ("../../../shared/generated.rs")`, comments between tokens, or `#[cfg_attr(unix, path = "../../../shared/module")]` are missed entirely. Files outside the initially scanned crate trees can therefore change without affecting the implementation-input hash.

Path deduplication occurs before propagating the reference's executable flag and crate origin. Consequently, an extensionless `include!` target already collected under `src` is never scanned for its own references, and a shared included source reached from two crates is scanned under only one `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` origin. Either case can omit compiled nested inputs from the hash.

`concat!` records only a boolean indicating that `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` appeared and discards its position and multiplicity. The resolver is correct when a single `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")` is the first component, but valid expressions with a literal before it or multiple occurrences resolve to a different workspace path than rustc uses. If that incorrectly resolved path exists, the actual compiled input is omitted from the hash.

Every escape in an ordinary string or character literal is rejected instead of decoded. On Windows, a normal valid reference such as `include_bytes!("..\\fixtures\\data.bin")` necessarily contains escaped backslashes, so implementation-input acquisition fails for common native-path syntax even though the resolver otherwise contains Windows-specific path handling.

The recursive `git ls-tree` result is fully buffered before `MAX_SOURCE_ENTRIES` is checked; the preliminary source-tree presence probe does not check the count at all. A branch with a very large tree can therefore exhaust memory before the limit is applied. The entry limit is also reset for each crate traversal, unlike the local collector's cumulative bound.

The new bounded blob reader protects implementation-input blobs, but the general merge-gate adapter still obtains specifications, catalogues, plans, rules, and signal documents through unbounded `fetch_blob_safe` calls. Those calls buffer the complete `git show` output before UTF-8 or schema decoding, so a maliciously large branch artifact can exhaust memory. These reads should use artifact-specific limits through the bounded helper as well.

Source-reference discovery requires `(` after an include macro, but Rust also permits `[]` and `{}` delimiters. A valid `include_bytes!["../../schema.bin"]` is skipped, so an external asset can change without invalidating the implementation-input hash. Recognize all valid macro delimiters.

`raw_string_bounds` recognizes only an `r` prefix, so `source_tokens` mis-lexes valid raw byte strings such as `br#"..."#`. Quotes inside such a literal can cause the lexer to swallow a subsequent `include_str!` invocation, omitting its referenced file from the hash. Handle raw byte-string prefixes atomically.

Local source paths are hashed using native `OsStr` bytes, while branch paths come from Git with `/` separators. On Windows, identical inputs therefore hash `libs\...` locally and `libs/...` on the branch; source-origin matching also fails for those native paths. Normalize local source and dependency-manifest paths to repository-style UTF-8 paths before hashing.

`char_literal_end` does not consume complete hexadecimal or Unicode escapes: for `'\x2f'` it checks for the closing quote at the first hex digit, and for `'\u{2f}'` it checks at `}` rather than after it. Valid references such as `include!(concat!("..", '\x2f', "generated.rs"))` are consequently rejected.

Every `path =` token nested anywhere in an attribute is treated as Rust's built-in module-path attribute. Valid procedural attributes such as `#[route(path = "/health")]` therefore produce an absolute-input error, and inactive `cfg_attr` alternatives are required unconditionally. Restrict discovery to the built-in `#[path = ...]` form and correctly adjudicate conditional path attributes.

Manifest-declared target and build-script paths are normalized against the workspace, but this additional crate-prefix check rejects valid workspace-local paths containing `..`, such as `[lib] path = "../../shared_api.rs"`. Both local and branch hashing then fail even though Cargo can compile the target. Retain the workspace-root boundary without requiring the file to remain under the package directory.

A textual include invocation whose argument is not immediately a literal or supported `concat!` is treated as an error. This rejects valid `macro_rules!` wrappers such as `($path:literal) => { include_str!($path) }`, where substitution makes the built-in invocation literal before expansion. Use expansion-aware dependency discovery or another conservative mechanism that supports include wrappers.

`raw_string_bounds` recognizes `r` and `br` literals but not valid `cr` raw C-string literals. A raw C string containing an unescaped quote is consequently tokenized as ordinary Rust syntax, which can produce an authoritative-input error or hide later source references, preventing reliable hashing of valid crates.

Macro-wrapper candidates are always marked non-executable. For example, a wrapper expanding to `include!($path)` will hash the first included file but never scan that file for nested `include!` or `#[path]` inputs, so changes to transitively compiled files can leave the implementation-input digest unchanged.

The fallback interprets string literals from every non-built-in macro as optional file paths. Valid unrelated code such as `vec![".."]` resolves to an existing directory, after which the optional reader fails because it is not a regular file; thus ordinary valid Rust can make local and branch input evaluation fail.

Macro literal candidates are neither deduplicated nor capped. Repeated missing literals do not increase `source_files`, so they bypass `MAX_SOURCE_FILES`; branch verification performs a separate Git lookup for each candidate, allowing one bounded source file to trigger hundreds of thousands of subprocesses and effectively exhaust the merge gate.

The newly accepted manifest-declared source paths outside their crate are assigned an origin from their physical location. A target such as `[lib] path = "../../shared.rs"` therefore receives the workspace root or another crate as its `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` origin, causing `concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), ...)` references to hash the wrong file or fail even though the crate builds.

Manifest-declared source files may now live outside their crate root, but reference discovery does not follow ordinary `mod child;` declarations. For `[lib] path = "../../shared/lib.rs"`, `shared/lib.rs` is selected while its implicitly loaded `shared/child.rs` is not, so changing that compiled module leaves the implementation-input hash unchanged.

When a built-in include has an unsupported but valid argument expression, `parse_reference_tokens` returns `None` and the caller silently ignores it. For example, an `include_str!(concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/assets/", env!("SCHEMA_FILE")))` input affects rustdoc but is neither hashed nor rejected, permitting stale cache reuse.

Macro-wrapper discovery is confined to definitions and invocations in the same file and assumes the invocation's literal is the final path. A wrapper defined in another module is missed entirely, while a same-file wrapper expanding to `include_str!(concat!("assets/", $path))` hashes the call-site literal instead of `assets/<literal>`; changes to the actual included asset therefore do not invalidate the hash.

Every lexically encountered built-in include is emitted as required without accounting for cfg removal or whether a macro body is expanded. A valid target containing `#[cfg(test)] const DATA: &str = include_str!("missing");` or an unused macro with such an include fails implementation-input evaluation even though rustdoc never accesses that path.

Executable-source origins are stored as a single `path -> crate_root` value, so a later crate overwrites an earlier origin when two workspace crates declare the same source file. That file is scanned under only one `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`; references resolved for the other crate are omitted, allowing their compiled inputs to change without changing the digest.

Every non-built-in macro invocation is treated as an include-wrapper candidate, even when its name is absent from `wrappers`, and nonexistent candidates still count toward the 256-entry limit. A valid source containing 257 unique `println!`, logging, or formatting literals therefore makes both local and branch implementation hashing fail. Restrict candidate collection and its limit to actual include wrappers, or count only successfully loaded references.

Wrapper reconstruction concatenates each body literal independently with the invocation literal. For a wrapper such as `include_str!(concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/assets/", $name, ".json"))`, it never constructs the actual `assets/<name>.json` path. Assets outside the initially scanned source tree are consequently omitted from the implementation hash, allowing stale signals after they change.

Recursive inline-module discovery discards the enclosing module names. When an executable source outside the recursively scanned crate roots contains `mod outer { mod child; }`, Rust resolves a path containing `outer/child`, while this code emits only paths for `child`. The actual module can therefore be omitted from both implementation hashes.

Whether an include is conditional is inferred from a file-wide substring search. An unrelated `#[cfg]`, `cfg_attr`, or `macro_rules` occurrence—even in a comment—causes every unresolved active include in the file to be silently skipped. For example, an active include using a second compile-time `env!` component is no longer rejected and its referenced input is never hashed. Conditionality must be determined per invocation; unresolved active references must fail closed.

All `.rs` files found anywhere under the crate directory are marked executable, including files unreachable from every Cargo target. The reference scanner consequently treats their includes as authoritative: an otherwise valid crate with an unreferenced `src/unused.rs` containing `include!("missing.rs")` now fails implementation hashing even though Cargo and rustdoc never load that file. Seed execution from declared target roots and traverse reachable modules/includes instead.

Every include inside a `cfg`-attributed item is treated as optional without evaluating the predicate. An always-active item such as `#[cfg(all())]` containing an otherwise unresolved `include_str!(concat!(..., env!(...)))` is silently skipped, so the referenced input never participates in either implementation hash. Active unresolved references must fail closed.

Conditional-range discovery visits only `syn::Item`. Rust permits `#[cfg]` on blocks, statements, impl members, and other non-Item nodes; an always-disabled block containing `include!("missing.rs")` is therefore scanned as active and makes hashing fail even though rustc removes it. Traverse all attribute-bearing syntax nodes.

Default Cargo roots are seeded solely from path shape, ignoring explicit target paths and `auto*` manifest flags. With `[lib] path = "src/actual.rs"`, an otherwise-unused `src/lib.rs` is still treated as executable; a missing include in that ignored file blocks both local and branch hashing although Cargo never loads it. Derive automatic roots from the manifest's target-discovery semantics.

Macro template extraction returns the first include found anywhere in the macro body and ignores arm selection. For a multi-arm wrapper whose first arm includes `a.json` and whose matching arm includes `assets/<argument>.json`, every invocation is resolved using the first arm, omitting the actual asset from the hash.

Invocation resolution takes the first literal in the invocation rather than the literal bound to the metavariable used by the include template. A wrapper such as `($label:literal, $path:literal) => include_str!($path)` hashes the label as a path and omits the second argument's actual file.

Macro templates are collapsed into one global map keyed only by macro name, with the first definition winning. This ignores Rust macro scope and makes duplicate names select an unrelated template; local filesystem enumeration is also unsorted while branch enumeration is sorted, so identical trees can select different templates and produce incompatible or incomplete hashes. Preserve origin/scope or fail closed on ambiguity.

The optional-source directory error path invokes `git_ls_tree_recursive_regular_files`, which captures recursive `git ls-tree` output without a byte or entry bound merely to report the entry count. Since the branch ref is not pinned between earlier probes and this call, a retargeted large tree can cause unbounded allocation. Reject the directory directly or use the bounded tree reader.

A `[lib]` table without an explicit `path` still makes Cargo compile `src/lib.rs`, but this condition suppresses that default root. Its source-reference traversal never runs, so changes to non-Rust files outside `src` referenced by that library can leave the implementation-input hash unchanged and permit stale signal reuse. Seed the effective default path when `[lib].path` is absent.

Each macro argument is reduced to the first string literal found anywhere inside it. For example, a wrapper invoked with `concat!("assets/", "schema.json")` is recorded as `assets/`, while the compiler reads `assets/schema.json`; because the candidate is optional, the actual external asset can be omitted from the hash. Resolve supported nested expressions exactly or reject them as ambiguous.

Macro templates are snapshotted before source-reference closure expansion and never updated. If an executable source uses `include!` to load an outside-`src` file that defines a wrapper macro, then invokes that macro afterward, the defining file is discovered too late and the original caller is never reprocessed. Assets referenced by that invocation can therefore be omitted from both local and branch hashes.

A branch-controlled directory at an optional build-script path triggers `git_ls_tree_recursive_regular_files` merely to format its entry count. That helper captures the complete recursive `git ls-tree` output without the new bounded collector, allowing a large tree to exhaust memory before the fail-closed directory error is returned. Reject the directory immediately or use bounded enumeration.

Pathless `[[bin]]` targets are always mapped to `src/bin/<name>.rs`, but Cargo can resolve a package-named explicit binary to `src/main.rs`. Since the presence of `[[bin]]` also disables automatic binary discovery here, `src/main.rs` is not queued for source-reference traversal. Consequently, external files referenced only by that binary can change without invalidating the implementation-input hash, allowing stale type signals through the merge gate.

When an optional source such as the implicit `build.rs` is a directory, this branch invokes `git_ls_tree_recursive_regular_files` merely to count its entries. That helper captures the entire recursive `git ls-tree` output without the surrounding `MAX_TREE_OUTPUT_BYTES` or entry limits, so a large branch tree can consume unbounded memory before the request fails closed. Reject the directory immediately or use the bounded enumeration path.

When an optional source such as the implicit `build.rs` is a directory, this branch recursively enumerates it solely to count entries. `git_ls_tree_recursive_regular_files` captures the complete `git ls-tree` output through unbounded `spawn_git`, bypassing this module's output and entry limits. A large branch tree can therefore exhaust memory before the adapter fails closed; reject the directory immediately or use bounded enumeration.

For edition-2018+ packages, declaring one `[[bin]]` does not disable Cargo's automatic binary discovery; only `autobins = false` does. This condition therefore omits other real `src/main.rs` or `src/bin/*` roots whenever any explicit binary exists. External inputs referenced only by an omitted binary are not traversed and can change without invalidating the implementation-input hash. Derive this default from Cargo's edition and `autobins` semantics.

A `syn::parse_file` failure is silently interpreted as having no ordinary modules. The evaluator accepts nightly Rust, while the bundled `syn` does not parse every nightly construct such as gen blocks; a valid root using such syntax can therefore leave its `mod child;` files unqueued for reference traversal. Non-Rust or out-of-tree inputs referenced by those compiled modules are then omitted from the hash. Propagate parser failure as an authoritative-input error or use a parser covering the accepted language.

`git ls-tree <ref> -- <path>` also returns no entry when an ancestor is a committed symlink or submodule, but this treats that result as an absent optional source. For optional module or conditional-reference paths outside the initially enumerated crate tree, the branch evaluator silently skips the unsafe boundary while local evaluation rejects it. Probe and reject every ancestor before accepting `NotFound`, as the existing ADR branch reader does.

For edition-2018+ packages, declaring one `[[bin]]` does not disable Cargo's automatic binary discovery; only `autobins = false` does. This condition therefore omits other real `src/main.rs` or `src/bin/*` roots whenever any explicit binary exists. External inputs referenced only by an omitted binary can change without invalidating the implementation-input hash. Derive this default from Cargo's edition and `autobins` semantics.

A `syn::parse_file` failure is silently interpreted as having no ordinary modules. The evaluator accepts nightly Rust, while `syn` does not parse every nightly construct; a valid root using such syntax can therefore leave its `mod child;` files unqueued for reference traversal. Non-Rust or out-of-tree inputs referenced by those compiled modules are then omitted from the hash. Propagate parser failure as an authoritative-input error or use a parser covering the accepted language.

`git ls-tree <ref> -- <path>` also returns no entry when an ancestor is a committed symlink or submodule, but this treats that result as an absent optional source. For optional module or conditional-reference paths outside the initially enumerated crate tree, the branch evaluator silently skips the unsafe boundary while local evaluation rejects it. Probe and reject every ancestor before accepting `NotFound`, as the existing ADR branch reader does.

The implementation-input hash passes `architecture-rules.json`'s `module_limits.exclude` entries into both tree walkers, so files excluded only for module-size measurement are omitted from the hash even though the adopted contract requires hashing each selected crate's entire directory tree. A change to (for example) a compiled/generated file under an excluded subtree can therefore reuse stale type signals.

The local tree walker joins the configured crate path to `workspace_root` and only checks the final component with `symlink_metadata`; symlinked ancestors such as `libs -> /outside` are followed by `read_dir`, allowing implementation inputs outside the trusted workspace to influence the hash and breaking local/branch parity. Reject symlinks up to the trusted workspace root before traversing each configured crate root.

The new branch implementation-input digest path calls `git_show_blob`, which uses the non-isolated `spawn_git` and inherits repository-selecting environment variables and history rewrites. Consequently, `branch_source_tree` enumerates paths from the isolated repository but hashes their contents from an ambient Git view; replacement objects or `GIT_DIR` can produce a digest that does not represent the target branch and potentially allow stale signals to match.

`fetch_branch_blob_limited` performs the symlink/submodule mode check with non-isolated `git_ls_tree_entry_kind`, then fetches content from the isolated repository. Ambient Git configuration or replacement objects can make the probe report a regular file while the target branch contains a symlink, causing the adapter to accept that blob and bypass its fail-closed symlink rejection. Use `git_ls_tree_entry_kind_isolated` for this verdict-bearing probe.

`hash_implementation_inputs_with_toolchain_identifier` now interprets `target_crate` as an architecture layer ID via `crate_roots_for`, but local callers still pass `binding.targets()[0]` (the schema-export target), while branch hashing passes `layer_id`. The binding contract allows those names to differ, so a valid configuration either fails local evaluation with “target layer not present” or hashes a different closure from the merge gate. Pass the binding's layer ID separately for graph selection and retain the schema-export target only for rustdoc invocation.

The canonical tree hash includes only each file's path and content digest, discarding the `100644` versus `100755` mode that branch enumeration already reads. That mode affects build semantics when a build script executes a checked-in helper: a mode-only change can make clean rustdoc extraction behave differently or fail while leaving `implementation_input_hash` unchanged and permitting stale signal reuse. Include the executable bit in `TreeFileDigest` and hash it identically on local and branch paths.

The v3 digest discards the rustdoc target after resolving it to a layer. Because architecture-rules.json is not itself hashed, changing a layer's sole schema_export target between two targets in the same crate tree leaves the cache key unchanged, allowing local cache reuse and branch-gate acceptance of signals generated for the old target. Include the canonical target identity in the shared hash and supply the binding target branch-side.

The non-Unix executable check always returns false, while branch hashing maps committed Git mode 100755 to true. A selected tree containing an executable file therefore produces incompatible local and branch hashes on Windows, permanently failing freshness checks. Derive the canonical Git executable bit or fail closed when it cannot be obtained.

The local depth calculation counts the leading slash left by strip_prefix, making every nested directory one level deeper than the branch calculation. With MAX_SOURCE_DEPTH=32, a file below 31 directories is rejected locally but accepted branch-side as exactly 32 components. Use the same file-relative depth definition on both paths.

`crate_root` may end with `/` because `validate_layer_path` accepts trailing separators. For such a root, `git ls-tree ... -- libs/foo/` lists the directory's children instead of the directory entry, so this probe classifies the first child (normally `Cargo.toml`) as `RegularFile` and rejects the branch. Local hashing accepts and traverses the same path, breaking local/branch parity for an accepted architecture-rules configuration. Normalize or reject trailing separators before probing.

`Path::components()` collapses repeated separators, so a path such as `libs//domain` still passes validation and local traversal. Git emits canonical `libs/domain/...` paths, causing `branch_tree_paths` to reject them at its literal prefix check; the merge gate therefore fails for a configuration accepted locally. Canonicalize paths before storing and duplicate detection, or reject all non-canonical separators.

findings.message: GO-01 adds the requirement that cleanup use the exact merged base commit, but its cited decisions are the original ADR D1 and cleanup-state ADR D3. Those decisions establish cleanup and ordering, respectively; the exact-commit requirement is defined by cleanup-state ADR D1/D2, neither of which GO-01 cites. This leaves part of the goal unanchored to its cited decision set.

CN-04 says any hash mismatch must trigger reevaluation and atomic cache replacement, but then says a present mismatched baseline must fail closed; AC-08 and AC-09 repeat these incompatible outcomes. Because a baseline-hash mismatch satisfies both clauses and neither is qualified by operation, downstream tests cannot determine whether to self-heal or reject. Distinguish evaluator cache misses from validation-gate mismatches and define the outcome for each authority.

`BaseMergeError::SourceMismatch` declares a `requested` branch, but `BaseMergeCommand` contains only `workspace_root` and the context port derives the source from the authoritative snapshot. No declared caller possesses a caller-selected branch to populate `requested`, making this error variant dead/unconstructible. Use a mismatch error whose payload reflects data available at the guard failure point.
